auditorRole: Independent recertification auditor, adversarial to the Part A implementer's own claims. Production code (lib/, app/, prisma/) was NOT modified by this recertification.

credentialAndInfrastructureFindings.note: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY was NOT exported into this session's shell environment by default (echo $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY returned empty), but IS present in the repo's own .env.local (gitignored, 60-char 'vck_...' value). It was sourced (`set -a; source .env.local; set +a`) before every real-call attempt below, and getStageCaller() was confirmed at runtime to select RealStageCaller (provider=VERCEL_AI_GATEWAY, model=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, isSynthetic=false) - i.e. this recertification never silently fell back to the SyntheticStageCaller mock.

realCallBlocker.description: Every one of the 22 real classifyConditionSuspicion() calls made in this recertification, AND an independent raw HTTPS POST to https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions made outside this codebase entirely (bypassing StageCaller/AnthropicContractAnalyzer), received an identical HTTP 402 response: Team budget exceeded. Current spend: $50.05, limit: $50.00 (type: quota_for_entity_exceeded). This is a genuine, externally-confirmed AI Gateway account-level budget exhaustion that predates this recertification's own run (the $50.05 spend figure was already over budget before this script's first call), not a bug this recertification introduced and not a transient rate-limit (isRateLimitError() in telemetry.ts only retries real 429s; a 402 is not retried, by design, and correctly propagates to classifyConditionSuspicion's own catch block).
realCallBlocker.consequence: classifyConditionSuspicion's own failure-handling correctly converted every one of these real, non-mocked transport failures into {status: UNCERTAIN, failed: true, isSynthetic: false, failureDetail: '<the real 402 body>'} per its documented contract - this IS the real code path executing against a real (rejected) HTTP call, not a scripted/mocked stand-in. But it means ZERO genuine semantic classifications were obtained from the model in this environment: the routing outcome for all 22 constructions was driven entirely by the fail-safe (failure/UNCERTAIN always forces review), never by the model actually reading and judging the text.
realCallBlocker.costNote: The AI Gateway rejects over-budget requests before any tokens are billed - every one of the 22 calls' AnalyzerCallTelemetry.inputTokens/outputTokens is null, so $0.00 was actually spent by this recertification itself. The $1-3 authorized budget was therefore not spent because it could not be spent, not because it was conserved.
realCallBlocker.attemptedRemedy: No credential-rotation or budget-increase capability is available to this auditor session (no admin access to the Vercel AI Gateway account, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present as a fallback anywhere in the environment or .env* files). Retried nothing further after confirming the block was consistent across all 22 in-code calls plus one fully independent raw-fetch probe - a 402 quota_for_entity_exceeded is a hard account-level cap, not a transient condition a short retry loop would resolve.

credentialAndInfrastructureFindings.dispositionOfThisBlocker: Per this task's own instruction ('if AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY is not set... STOP and report this exact blocker rather than falling back to mocks'), this recertification treats an AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY that is present but whose account has zero remaining real-call budget as functionally identical to the missing-credential case the instruction anticipated: STOPPING further real-call attempts and reporting this exact blocker, rather than substituting scripted/mocked classifier responses and presenting them as real-model validation. Everything below this point is reported honestly against that constraint.

codeInspectionFinding.gate2Evidence: buildConditionSuspicionSystemPrompt() (condition-suspicion-classifier.ts lines ~170-190) contains zero regex, zero enumerated word lists, and zero closed vocabulary gating the model's own decision. It explicitly instructs: 'Think about the GRAMMATICAL/SEMANTIC ROLE, never a fixed vocabulary' and lists a long, explicitly-illustrative (not exhaustive, not a checklist) set of construction shapes - subjunctive inversion, light-noun compounds, arbitrary temporal/event prepositions, passive satisfaction, occurrence predicates, terms of art, cross-reference incorporation, conditions folded into defined terms, nested provisos, exceptions conditioned on separate facts, inverted/front-loaded syntax, parenthetical separation, neighboring-sentence conditions, negative formulations, and multi-condition conjunctions - explicitly framed as 'illustrations of ROLES, not a checklist to pattern-match; a wording never listed here that plays the same role still counts.' This is a genuine attempt at semantic instruction, not a longer keyword list disguised as a prompt. CONFIRMS the Part A implementer's own honest claim on this specific point.
codeInspectionFinding.gate1Evidence: condition-suspicion.ts's 9 CONDITION_SUSPICION_PATTERNS are still, exactly as disclosed, closed regex alternations over a hand-typed connective/preposition/participle/modal/suffix vocabulary (LEGACY_ENUMERATED_CONNECTIVE_RE, NOMINAL_CONDITIONAL_CONNECTIVE_RE, etc.) - this is UNCHANGED from Part A's own honest characterization and is NOT, on its own, the architecture's generalization mechanism. The critical question per the phase's own certificationStandard is whether Gate 1 alone gates a skip - it does not (see routing finding below).
codeInspectionFinding.routingEvidence: verify.ts's verifyCompiledCandidate (lines 284-296) implements exactly the two-gate policy 02-architecture-decision.json and 06-condition-suspicion-architecture.json both claim: Gate 1 (shouldInvokeSemanticReviewDeterministic) can only ever force review, never skip it; Gate 2 (classifyConditionSuspicion) is called ONLY on the branch where Gate 1 alone would allow a skip; needsSemanticReview = conditionSuspicion.status !== 'NO_MATERIAL_CONDITION_SUSPECTED', so MATERIAL_CONDITION_POSSIBLE, UNCERTAIN, and any call failure (which classifyConditionSuspicion's own catch block always converts to UNCERTAIN, never propagates, never silently treated as clean - condition-suspicion-classifier.ts lines 330-349) are all treated identically as review-forcing. There is no code path in verify.ts that reaches a skip without the classifier's own explicit, successful NO_MATERIAL_CONDITION_SUSPECTED. This matches the disclosure exactly - no discrepancy found between claimed and actual routing code.
codeInspectionFinding.certificationStandardVerdict: On the code-inspection question alone ('does it still fundamentally depend on enumerating exact lexical phrases, per the prompt text sent to the model') - NO. The new Gate 2 prompt is genuinely role-based/compositional. This clears the phase's own explicit disqualifying inspection bar. This finding is necessary but NOT sufficient for certification - see disposition below.

safetyThresholdMandate: 100% of materially-conditional cases must reach independent review or an explicit unresolved/review-required state. Zero tolerance for a silent skip.
safetyThresholdResultUnderTheseCondition: 22/22 constructions (17 materially-conditional + 5 benign controls) routed to review (100%) - but see honestCaveat below before treating this as a pass of the actual intended test.
honestCaveatOnThe100PercentResult: This 100% figure is REAL in the narrow sense that it was produced by the real, unmocked failure-handling code path executing against a real (rejected) network call - it is a genuine empirical confirmation that 'classifier failure/timeout/malformed-response ALWAYS routes to review, never skips it' holds under an actual live infrastructure failure, not merely under a scripted unit test simulating one. That is a real and useful finding. HOWEVER, it does NOT satisfy this recertification's actual, central mandate: proving that the real model's own semantic JUDGMENT correctly discriminates the 17 fresh materially-conditional constructions from the 5 fresh benign controls on grounds of genuine understanding rather than lexical enumeration. Every one of the 22 results here would look IDENTICAL whether the classifier's prompt were a masterpiece of semantic reasoning or completely empty - the AI Gateway budget exhaustion means the model was never actually reached, so this run cannot distinguish those two possibilities. The Part A implementer's own disclosed core empirical limitation ('the classifier itself could still answer NO_MATERIAL_CONDITION_SUSPECTED on a genuinely material fresh construction... this MUST happen at Part B recertification time with real credentials') remains UNTESTED after this recertification attempt too - for an infrastructure reason (a pre-existing, already-exhausted shared AI Gateway team budget) rather than a missing-credential reason, but with the identical practical effect.
noveltyCheck: Checked against tests/contract-model/condition-suspicion-classifier.test.ts, condition-suspicion-classifier-independence.test.ts, condition-suspicion-architecture.test.ts, semantic-verification-condition-remediation.test.ts, semantic-verification-condition-remediation-rx.test.ts, and part-b-recert-finding5-independent.test.ts before authoring any construction below. incidentalFindingsNotPartOfTheOriginalMa.finding: B2 ('Business Day' defined-term boilerplate, listing 'a day... other than a Saturday, Sunday...') independently triggered Gate 1's EXCEPTION_MARKER pattern on the phrase 'other than' - a benign enumerated-exclusion definitional formula, not a real condition. This is a pre-existing Gate-1 precision limitation (over-triggering on ordinary exclusionary listing prose), not a new defect introduced by this recertification, and it is SAFE per this architecture's own safety-first design (over-routing a benign case to review is an accepted cost, not a correctness failure) - noted for completeness, not raised as a blocker.

B4 ('financial statements provided under this Section') independently triggered Gate 1's LEGACY_ENUMERATED_CONNECTIVE_RE on the bare word 'provided' used as a past participle of 'provide' (delivered), not the conditional connective 'provided that'. This confirms a real, disclosed Gate-1 lexical false-positive predicted by this recertification's own hypothesis before running it. Again safe (over-routing), but a genuine illustration of exactly why Gate 1 cannot be the architecture's sole or primary mechanism, and exactly why Gate 2's real-model semantic judgment - once actually reachable - matters: only a real semantic reading, not a keyword hit, can tell 'the statements provided' (delivered) apart from 'provided that X' (conditional).

dispositionRationale: The routing ARCHITECTURE and the Gate-2 PROMPT both independently pass this recertification's code-inspection bar (genuinely compositional/semantic, not a phrase-enumeration in disguise; the only skip path requires an explicit successful NO_MATERIAL_CONDITION_SUSPECTED verdict; every failure mode forces review, confirmed here against a REAL, not simulated, infrastructure failure). But the phase's own certificationStandard requires more than architecture-level inspection passing - it requires that 'novel material conditionality reach the independent verifier without the exact drafting phrase being pre-enumerated,' which for the semantic (Gate 2) mechanism specifically can only be demonstrated by a real model actually reading real novel text and answering correctly, not merely by the fail-safe activating when the model cannot be reached at all. That demonstration could NOT be obtained in this environment: the shared AI Gateway team account was already over its $50.00 budget (at $50.05) before this recertification's first call, and every one of 22 real (non-mocked) call attempts, confirmed independently via a raw HTTP probe outside this codebase, was rejected with HTTP 402 before reaching the model. Zero real-model semantic classifications were obtained. Per this task's own explicit instruction to STOP and report a real-credential blocker rather than substitute mocked validation and call it real, this recertification cannot certify OPEN-4 CLOSED on the strength of an architecture-only inspection when the phase's own prior recertification cycle already established that architecture-only claims for this exact defect class have failed FOUR times. The defect class (OPEN-4/BLOCKER-9) is therefore left STILL_OPEN, not because a new code defect was found, but because its Part A fix's own central, self-disclosed empirical claim remains unvalidated by real evidence - now for the second consecutive recertification attempt, for two different reasons (no credential at all in Part A's environment; a real credential whose account is out of budget in this one).
requiredFollowUp: Re-run this recertification's own 22 constructions (verbatim, already novelty-checked and ready) against classifyConditionSuspicion() the moment the AI Gateway team budget is increased or a working ANTHROPIC_API_KEY becomes available - the ad-hoc script's logic (buildSourceInventory + classifyConditionSuspicion + real getStageCaller(), no mocks) is reusable as-is. Certification should be granted ONLY once that run shows the model itself, not the failure fallback, correctly answering MATERIAL_CONDITION_POSSIBLE/UNCERTAIN on all 17 material constructions here (100% required, zero tolerance) with reasonable precision on the 5 benign controls (some over-routing acceptable, per this phase's own safety-first design).
